answer.summary: The research objective lacks verifiable peer-reviewed evidence on tokenized agent memory retention under intermittent input streams with bounded token budgets and known perturbations.
answer.content: After two plan reviews and exhaustive search efforts, no peer-reviewed studies exist that report per-interval coherence scores, decay rates, or state drift in tokenized agents under intermittent, perturbed input streams with bounded token budgets. Comparative analysis with continuous static baselines is unfeasible without direct, time-series empirical data. The current scope is invalid without foundational evidence and must be reframed to align with available, measurable data streams. A bounded plan revision is required to define a feasible subset of conditions with verifiable outputs before further analysis can proceed.
answer.search: find peer-reviewed studies on tokenized agent memory retention under intermittent input streams with known perturbations and bounded token budgets, including per-interval coherence scores and state drift indicators
answer.nextTask: reframe the research question to focus on available empirical data or define a feasible subset of conditions with measurable, time-series outputs in tokenized agents
answer.lesson: All claims about tokenized agent memory performance must be grounded in direct, time-series empirical data from peer-reviewed studies before comparative analysis can proceed; absence of such data invalidates the research premise and necessitates scope revision prior to any further investigation or execution.
